seo.description: Complete guide to Law in Ireland for Indian students: Top Irish universities, eligibility criteria, tuition fees (€13,500 – €28,640 / year), scholarships, and 2-year post-study work visa (Stamp 1G).

overview: Study Law in Ireland is a popular choice for students interested in legal systems, human rights, business regulations, public policy and justice. Ireland has undergraduate law degrees, postgraduate law programmes and specialized qualifications in fields like international law, corporate law, human rights and intellectual property.
After secondary school, students may decide to pursue a law degree; after a bachelor’s degree, they may decide to pursue postgraduate legal studies.
But studying law and qualifying to practise as a solicitor or barrister in Ireland are two different things. Students must know the professional requirements when choosing a program.
Edu Hawk consultancy University selection guidance helps students compare suitable institutions based on their academic background, budget, preferred location and long-term professional goals.

items: Students who want to learn about legal principles, develop analytical skills and pursue a career in legal services or a related field will find a great range of law programs available in Ireland.
Key benefits are:
- Strong academic foundation: Study constitutional law, criminal law, contract law, property law and legal research.
- International perspectives: Explore European law, international law, human rights and cross-border legal issues.
- Specialised postgraduate options: Specialize in areas including business law, technology law, maritime law and dispute resolution.
- Transferable skills: Learn critical thinking, communication, negotiation, research and problem-solving skills.
- Career flexibility: Options in legal practice, compliance, corporate services, public administration and policy.
- Education in English: Most programs are taught in English, which can help international students to develop professional legal communication skills.
Irish institutions provide law courses at undergraduate, post-graduate and professional levels.
Law courses for undergrad
These are generally programs for students who have completed Class 12 or equivalent qualification.
Typical choices are:
LLB (Bachelor of Law)
BCL (Canon Law)
BCL Law & Business
French or other language with Law
Law with History, Politics or Philosophy
Human Rights & Law
Law & Criminal Justice
Undergraduate law degrees generally take three to four years depending on the course. Some courses offer an extra year of language study, an international pathway or another specialization.
Law postgraduate courses
Postgraduate law programmes are ideal for graduates wanting to develop their legal knowledge further or to specialize.
The most popular ones are:
Master of Laws (LLM)
International Human Rights LLM
LLM International Business Law
Master of Laws in Corporate Law
LLM Intellectual Property Law and Information Technology
LLM in Environmental Laws
LL.M. in Maritime Law
LLM Law of Technology and Innovation
Postgraduate Diploma in Legal Studies or legal specialization
Most full-time LLM programmes are one year long but part-time courses can take two years or more.
Non-law degree law courses
Some graduate-entry law programmes might be available to students who have a bachelor's degree in another subject.
Trinity College Dublin
University College Cork
University of Galway
Dublin City University

sections.title: 4. Eligibility for Study Law in Ireland

items: Depending on the curriculum, institution, and degree of qualification, you can study law in Ireland.
Undergraduate law eligibility
Applicants will normally need:
- A recognized secondary school qualification e.g. Class 12 for Indian applicants.
- Academic performance that meets the entry requirements of the institution in that country.
- Proof of proficiency in English, if applicable.
- Any subject prerequisites set by the university.
You don’t need to have studied law before for most undergraduate law degree courses. Some joint degrees may require knowledge of another subject or a specific language.
Postgraduate law eligibility
Most applicants will require:
- A recognized degree.
- Academic grades that fulfill the programme’s entry requirements.
- Proof of English language proficiency if required.
- Applicable legal studies or work experience where the course requires it.
Some LLM programmes require an undergraduate law degree, but others will accept graduates from related fields or those with relevant professional experience.
Who can study law at a post-graduate level?
Some graduate-entry LLB programmes are available to applicants with a non-law bachelor’s degree. These courses are offered for different periods of time and with different academic requirements.
Students should make sure that the course is designed for those who do not have a law degree, and that the qualification will be useful for their longer-term career goals.

sections.title: 5. Admission Requirements to Law in Ireland

items: Universities assess applicants based on academic qualifications, English-language proficiency and programme-specific requirements.
Typical admission requirements include:
- Transcripts and certificates: Documents indicating your previous qualifications and grades.
- English language requirements: Applicants may need to take IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic or other accepted tests. Schools require different scores.
- Statement of purpose: Some postgraduate courses will ask candidates to write about their interest in law, relevant experience and future career plans.
- CV or résumé This may be required for some postgraduate programs.
- References: Some schools require recommendations from academics or employers.
- Additional assessments: Some programmes may require an interview or further supporting documentation.
- Language proficiency: Joint degrees with French, Irish or other languages may have additional requirements.
Meeting minimum requirements does not assure admission. Applicants are advised to check the current course page and application deadlines before applying.

sections.title: 6. Cost of Study Law in Ireland

items: Law tuition fees in Ireland differ depending on the institution, program level, duration and student fee category. International students outside the EU usually pay different fees from eligible EU students.
Tuition fees (approximate)
Bachelor's in law \| €15,000-€25,000 \|
Postgraduate law degree \| €17,000–€30,000 \|
These are estimated budget numbers. The actual fees depend on the course and may be outside these ranges.
Published Fee Examples

University of Galway, undergraduate BCL Law: The published total non-EU fee is €19,390 per year including the levy.
University College Cork, undergraduate BCL Law entry routes: Published non-EU tuition is €21,700 annually plus a capitation fee.
University College Cork, selected LLM programmes: Published non-EU tuition fees are €19,700 for a one year full time program.
Cost of living
Students should also anticipate:
Housing and utilities
Groceries and food
Public transport
Books and materials for legal studies
Medical insurance, if applicable
Costs to yourself
Visa and immigration costs (where applicable)
Cost of living in Ireland depends on the city and type of accommodation. Students should create a separate budget for tuition and living expenses.
International students may be eligible for scholarships offered by individual institutions. Don’t expect funding to be awarded.

sections.title: 7. Law School Admission Process in Ireland

items: 01. The law admission process in Ireland usually involves the following steps:
02. Choose your study route: Select a undergraduate law degree, graduate-entry law course, LLM or specialized postgraduate program.
03. Research Universities: Course Modules, Duration, Fees & Career Relevance.
04. Check you are eligible: You must meet the academic qualifications and English language requirements.
05. Gather documents: Collect transcripts, certificates, passport details and any other supporting documents required.
06. Apply: Apply through the university's official portal or the way prescribed by the institution.
07. Submit payment: Pay the required application fee.
08. Reply to admission requests: Provide any additional information required.
09. Look over the offer: Review the terms and conditions, tuition payments, deposit requirements and deadlines.
10. Find funding and housing: Budget for tuition and living costs.
11. Immigration formalities: If you require student visa or immigration permission, please adhere to the current official requirements.

sections.title: 8. Professional and Law Accreditation Recognition in Ireland

items: If you’re thinking about studying a law course in Ireland, you’ll want to ensure the institution is recognized, and that the qualification you’ll receive is appropriate for your career plans.
Things to consider:
- Institution recognition: Check that the university provides the qualification stated on the course page.
- National Framework of Qualifications: Check the level of the qualification where appropriate.
- Quality and Qualifications Ireland (QQI): Learn about Irish qualifications and quality assurance.
- Professional recognition: Verify that the qualification is recognized for the academic requirements of the relevant professional pathway.
Recognition abroad: If you are planning to work outside Ireland, check the rules of the country where you intend to work.
How to become a barrister in Ireland
King's Inns is the professional training body for those who wish to be barristers.
Applicants will normally need to have an approved legal qualification or other accepted route to meet the entrance requirements prior to undertaking the professional course.

sections.title: 9. Salary and Job Prospects after Law in Ireland

items: Opportunities for law graduates in Ireland include legal practice, corporate organisations, public administration, compliance, consulting and policy-related work. Positions available, dependent on qualification, experience and any professional registration required.
Popular career paths
Possible roles:
Legal Secretary
Legal assistant
Law Researcher
Compliance Analyst
Contract Administrator
Corporate Governance Assistant
Legal Executive
Researcher in Policy
Solicitor - meets professional requirements
Barrister, if professional requirements are satisfied
In-house Legal Counsel with relevant qualifications and experience

Some contract-related, compliance and legal support roles may be available without being qualified as a practising lawyer. Reserved legal services and regulated profession posts have further requirements.
Expected salary
The salary depends on the job title, the employer, the location, experience and professional qualification.
For some entry-level legal support and compliance roles you might be looking at €28,000-€40,000 annually as a rough planning figure.
Qualified lawyers and seasoned legal experts can earn substantially more depending on their practice area and employer.
Career Opportunities After Graduation
Graduation does not automatically give you the right to work or to stay in Ireland.
Graduates of eligible Irish higher education courses may be eligible to apply under the Third Level Graduate Programme subject to prevailing conditions.

sections.title: 10. Documents Required for Studying Law in Ireland

items: The exact list of documents varies between institutions and programs. Typical requirements are:
*Valid passport
- Certificates and transcripts of studies
-Applicable Class 10 and Class 12 documents for undergraduate candidates
- Certificate and transcripts of Bachelor’s degree for applicants for postgraduate programs
- Results of an English test, if available
- Statement of purpose where needed
- Résumé or CV, if applicable
- References (academic or professional, if required)
- Filled out application form
- Proof of payment for application fee, if applicable
- Financial evidence and any other documents required for the visa process, if applicable.
Certified copies, official translations or verification of academic documents may be required from applicants. Refer to separate university application instructions and immigration requirements.

faqs.q: 1\. Is Ireland a good country to study Law?
faqs.a: Ireland has a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate law programmes including Irish law, international law, business law and human rights. It may be suitable for students who wish to pursue a career in law and to work in Ireland or abroad, subject to the applicable professional requirements.

faqs.q: 2\. How many years does it take to study Law in Ireland?
faqs.a: Undergraduate law degrees generally take three to four years. Many full-time LLM courses take one year. Some graduate-entry degrees and combined programs have different lengths.

faqs.q: 3\. Can I do Law in Ireland after Class 12?
faqs.a: Yes. Students who have completed Class 12 or equivalent qualification can apply for eligible undergraduate law degrees if they meet the academic and English-language requirements of the university.

faqs.q: 4\. What is the cost of studying Law in Ireland?
faqs.a: Tuition will vary by university and program. As a rough guide, undergraduate law tuition fees can range from €15,000 to €25,000 a year, while postgraduate law tuition fees can range from €17,000 to €30,000 a year. Additional living costs.

faqs.q: 5\. Can I be a solicitor or barrister after studying Law in Ireland?
faqs.a: Yes, if you satisfy the appropriate professional and academic requirements The qualification process for solicitors is governed by the Law Society of Ireland and the qualification process for barristers is governed by King's Inns. It is not a case of a law degree automatically qualifying a graduate to practise.

faqs.q: How can Edu Hawk worldwide Consultancy help me to study abroad?
faqs.a: Edu Hawk worldwide assists students in finding the right universities, understanding admission requirements, handling application documents, and planning their study abroad journey.
